remaining.classification: same acceptance result with bounded pre-validation work difference
remaining.reason: Digit-only fields convert to nonnegative integers or Infinity; the finite maximum rejects Infinity. Removing the positive-integer conjunction can nevertheless let zero pass this early check. validateOptions rejects zero before native derivation, preserving verification decisions but allowing decoding and option construction before rejection. This is a bounded pre-validation work difference, not strict work equivalence.

remaining.classification: same acceptance result with bounded pre-validation work difference
remaining.reason: Weakening the positive integer predicate admits zero through the initial parameter check. The later validateOptions rejects zero and parseHash catches that error, so verify still returns false and needsRehash remains true. However salt/tag decoding can occur before rejection, unlike the original. Keep this validation-order/resource distinction visible; the unchanged maxEncodedHashChars cap bounds decoding work. It is not strict instruction/work equivalence.
